raw_case_text:
A 27-year-old male with no past medical history presented to the emergency department with headache for the past 2 days. He also endorsed photophobia, chills, night sweats, decreased appetite, 10-pound unintentional weight loss, and fevers. The patient reported being sexually active with men only with the last unprotected sexual intercourse 2 weeks ago. He denied any illicit drug use.
In the emergency department, the patient had a temperature of 38.2  C, a heart rate of 103 beats/minutes, respiratory rate of 20 breaths/minutes, blood pressure of 100/60 mm Hg, and O2 saturation of 100% on room air. Physical examination was unremarkable with no meningeal signs. Given his headache and a fever of 38.3  C, the patient was started on empiric meningitis treatment with vancomycin and ceftriaxone. Computed tomography of the head without contrast showed no acute intracranial process. Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain with and without contrast was unremarkable.
Initial laboratory findings (Table 1) were significant for leukopenia of 2.2 x 103/microL, thrombocytopenia of 81 x 103/microL, hemoglobin of 12.3 g/dL, transaminitis, elevated C-reactive protein of 3.16 mg/dL, and hypoalbuminemia. Chest X-ray did not reveal any active infection or any other pathology. Blood cultures were negative. Lumbar puncture revealed the following: white blood cells 3 cells/cm2, red blood cells 378 cells/cm2, glucose 54 mg/dL, and elevated protein 51 mg/dL. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) was negative for cryptococcal antigen, herpes simplex virus, and CSF VDRL. Accordingly, vancomycin was discontinued. Ceftriaxone was decreased to 1 g every 24 hours for 2 weeks, followed by intramuscular benzathine penicillin G 3 million units to treat presumed neurosyphilis due to elevated protein in the CSF. HIV antigen/antibody test was positive, with an HIV-RNA level over 10 000 000 copies/mL, CD4 T-cell count of 201 cells/microL, and CD8 T-cell count of 93 cells/microL. These results along with fatigue, fever, pancytopenia, and transaminitis supported the diagnosis of acute retroviral syndrome; therefore, ART was initiated consisting of darunavir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide.
Additional laboratory values (Tables 1 and 2) showed hyperferritinemia >40 000 ng/mL, D-dimer >5000 ng/dL, bi-cytopenia, transaminitis, and hypertriglyceridemia, which raised concern for HLH. H-score showed a 93% to 96% probability of having HLH (Table 3). A collaborative decision was made by the patient and the physicians to defer bone marrow biopsy and we chose to confirm our suspicion by performing noninvasive tests such as interleukin (IL)-2 receptor and natural killer (NK) cell activity.
Computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast showed borderline prominent right hepatic lobe, slight hypodensity of the liver suggesting fatty hepatocellular changes, and mesenteric adenitis. The patient's symptoms of headache had self-resolved on the third day of admission and he left against medical advice. Following discharge, IL-2R returned >4000 pg/mL. The suspicion of HLH secondary to acute HIV was confirmed as the patient met 4/8 criteria for the diagnosis including fever, bi-cytopenia of thrombocytopenia and neutropenia, elevated ferritin, elevated IL-2R along with the high probability of H-score. The patient followed-up outpatient and he reported complete resolution of his symptoms.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 27-year-old male presenting with headache, photophobia, chills, fever, night sweats, and weight loss for two days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 27-year-old male presented with a 2-day history of persistent headache accompanied by photophobia, subjective fevers, chills, night sweats, anorexia, and a 10-pound unintentional weight loss. Due to persistent headache and fevers reaching 38.3 °C, he was admitted to the emergency department for evaluation of suspected meningitis.
subjective.past_medical_history: No prior medical history; denies illicit drug use. Epidemiological risk: Sexually active with men only, reporting unprotected sexual intercourse two weeks prior to presentation.
subjective.review_of_systems: Headache, photophobia, chills, night sweats, decreased appetite, 10-pound unintentional weight loss, and fatigue; denies neck stiffness, rash, or focal weakness.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature 38.2 °C (fever up to 38.3 °C), heart rate 103 beats/min (tachycardia), respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, blood pressure 100/60 mmHg, oxygen saturation 100% on room air. Neurological: Normal examination, no meningeal signs or nuchal rigidity. General: Alert, oriented.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count: Leukopenia of 2.2 x 10^3/microL, thrombocytopenia of 81 x 10^3/microL, hemoglobin 12.3 g/dL. Serum biochemistry: Transaminitis, hypoalbuminemia, elevated C-reactive protein of 3.16 mg/dL, ferritin > 40,000 ng/mL, D-dimer > 5,000 ng/dL, hypertriglyceridemia. Blood cultures: Negative. Chest X-ray: No active pulmonary infection or pathology. Lumbar puncture: CSF WBC 3 cells/mm3, RBC 378 cells/mm3, glucose 54 mg/dL, protein elevated at 51 mg/dL; CSF cryptococcal antigen, HSV PCR, and VDRL were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Non-contrast CT head: No acute intracranial process. Brain MRI (with and without contrast): Unremarkable. Contrast-enhanced CT abdomen and pelvis: Borderline prominent right hepatic lobe, mild hepatic steatosis, and mesenteric adenitis. Serum soluble interleukin-2 receptor (sIL-2R): > 4,000 pg/mL. H-score: 93% to 96% probability of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Bone marrow biopsy: Deferred.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Acute retroviral syndrome (ARS) secondary to primary human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection complicated by secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH; met 4/8 diagnostic criteria with fever, bi-cytopenia, ferritin > 40,000 ng/mL, sIL-2R > 4,000 pg/mL, and H-score 93-96%) and presumed neurosyphilis.
Confirmatory Testing: Positive 4th-generation HIV antigen/antibody test, plasma HIV RNA > 10,000,000 copies/mL, CD4 T-cell count 201 cells/microL, CD8 T-cell count 93 cells/microL.
Treatment & Outcome: Initially treated empirically with vancomycin and ceftriaxone for meningitis; vancomycin stopped following negative CSF gram stain/cultures. Ceftriaxone was transitioned to 1 g IV daily for 2 weeks followed by benzathine penicillin G 3 million units IM for presumed neurosyphilis. Antiretroviral therapy (darunavir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide) was initiated. Headache resolved by day 3; the patient left against medical advice but attended outpatient follow-up with complete symptom resolution.
